VoipPhoneServiceEvent._has_pending_pbx_leg

Inputs and defaults: VoipPhoneServiceEvent._has_pending_pbx_leg(self, call).

Decorators/execution contract: @api.model. Read decorator implementations: they can wrap, register or replace this function.

Maintainer's function contract:

Whether a PBX channel of this call still owes its own hangup event.

The cancel only says the member stopped ringing: a group ring emits one
whether nobody picked up or a colleague did. The member's own
``call_ended`` is what carries the verdict, so a member with a live PBX
channel is settled by that event rather than by this guess — which,
processed concurrently with the winner's answer, reads it as absent and
lands on "missed". A member reached by push alone owns no PBX channel,
so there the cancel stays the settling signal.

Execution order (visible in this function, not inferred transitive effects):

  1. Return any((leg.pbx_call_id and (not leg.ended_at) for leg in call.leg_ids)); this branch ends here.
VoipPhoneServiceEvent._has_ring_window_elapsed

Inputs and defaults: VoipPhoneServiceEvent._has_ring_window_elapsed(self, payload).

Decorators/execution contract: @api.model. Read decorator implementations: they can wrap, register or replace this function.

Maintainer's function contract:

Whether the PBX has already stopped ringing for this push.

webhookd redelivers failed webhooks with backoff, so a push can arrive
minutes after the ring it announces; ringing the devices then would
offer a call that can no longer be answered. The matched or
bootstrapped call is kept so the (equally late) cancel can still
settle it as missed.

Execution order (visible in this function, not inferred transitive effects):

  1. Set ring_end from self._parse_naive_utc(payload['mobile_wakeup_timestamp']) + timedelta(seconds=int(payload['ring_timeout'])).
  2. Return fields.Datetime.now() > ring_end; this branch ends here.
VoipPhoneServiceEvent._ensure_pushed_call

Inputs and defaults: VoipPhoneServiceEvent._ensure_pushed_call(self, payload).

Decorators/execution contract: @api.model. Read decorator implementations: they can wrap, register or replace this function.

Maintainer's function contract:

Find-or-create the incoming call a push refers to.

A live call is reused when one of its keys resolves; otherwise it is
bootstrapped from the push.

A logged-out user's softphone is unregistered, so Wazo dials no callee
leg and no user-facing call exists — yet the push is the signal to ring
the browser anyway. The enriched push carries the target user_uuid and
conversation_id, which is all ``_ensure_user_call`` needs to build it.

A logged-in user's browser may instead have created the call from the
INVITE already. That INVITE carries X-Odoo-Conversation-Id (the
wazo-calld-odoo-push plugin stamps it on the dial_mobile dial), so the
call is keyed by the conversation id and ``_find_pushed_call`` above
already matched it.

Execution order (visible in this function, not inferred transitive effects):

  1. Set call from self._find_pushed_call(payload).
  2. Test call. If true:
    1. Return call; this branch ends here.
  3. Test not (payload.get('user_uuid') and payload.get('conversation_id')). If true:
    1. Return self.env['voip.call'].browse(); this branch ends here.
  4. Set conversation from self._ensure_conversation(payload).
  5. Return self._ensure_user_call(dict(payload, sip_call_id=''), conversation); this branch ends here.
VoipPhoneServiceEvent._find_pushed_call

Inputs and defaults: VoipPhoneServiceEvent._find_pushed_call(self, payload).

Decorators/execution contract: @api.model. Read decorator implementations: they can wrap, register or replace this function.

Maintainer's function contract:

Resolve the call a PBX push event refers to.

Only the enriched pair (user_uuid, conversation_id) identifies it. The
payload's own SIP Call-ID belongs to the channel that raised Pushmobile,
which on a direct call is the caller's (captured 2026-07-23) and never
the woken member's, so resolving through it binds a member's push to
somebody else's call.

Execution order (visible in this function, not inferred transitive effects):

  1. Set user_uuid from payload.get('user_uuid').
  2. Set conversation_id from payload.get('conversation_id').
  3. Test not (user_uuid and conversation_id). If true:
    1. Return self.env['voip.call']; this branch ends here.
  4. Set user from self.env['res.users']._get_from_pbx_user_uuid(user_uuid).
  5. Test not user. If true:
    1. Return self.env['voip.call']; this branch ends here.
  6. Return self.env['voip.call'].sudo().search([('control_handle', '=', conversation_id), ('user_id', '=', user.id), ('direction', '=', 'incoming'), ('state', 'in', LIVE_CALL_STATES)], limit=1); this branch ends here.
VoipPhoneServiceEvent._ensure_call_records

Inputs and defaults: VoipPhoneServiceEvent._ensure_call_records(self, payload, event_type, occurred_at).

Decorators/execution contract: @api.model. Read decorator implementations: they can wrap, register or replace this function.

Maintainer's function contract:

Find-or-create the {conversation, user call, leg} records this call event touches.

An event for any leg (or the browser INVITE) may arrive in any order, so
every lifecycle handler ensures the full trio exists before applying its
state effect.

Execution order (visible in this function, not inferred transitive effects):

  1. Set conversation from self._ensure_conversation(payload).
  2. Set call from self._ensure_user_call(payload, conversation).
  3. Set leg from self._ensure_leg(payload, conversation, call, event_type, occurred_at).
  4. Return (conversation, call, leg); this branch ends here.
VoipPhoneServiceEvent._ensure_conversation

Inputs and defaults: VoipPhoneServiceEvent._ensure_conversation(self, payload).

Decorators/execution contract: @api.model. Read decorator implementations: they can wrap, register or replace this function.

Execution order (visible in this function, not inferred transitive effects):

  1. Set conversation_id from payload['conversation_id'].
  2. Set ConversationSudo from self.env['voip.conversation'].sudo().
  3. Set conversation from ConversationSudo.search([('conversation_identifier', '=', conversation_id)], limit=1).
  4. Test not conversation. If true:
    1. Try these operations:
      1. Set conversation from ConversationSudo.create({'conversation_identifier': conversation_id}).

      On UniqueViolation:

      1. Raise ConcurrencyError(); follow the nearest applicable handler, not an assumed provider rollback.
  5. Return conversation; this branch ends here.
VoipPhoneServiceEvent._ensure_user_call

Inputs and defaults: VoipPhoneServiceEvent._ensure_user_call(self, payload, conversation).

Decorators/execution contract: @api.model. Read decorator implementations: they can wrap, register or replace this function.

Maintainer's function contract:

Find-or-create the user-facing call this leg belongs to.

Only a softphone endpoint leg owns a call; the inbound trunk/source leg
builds the conversation and its own leg but never a user-facing call — that
is created by the user legs and the browser INVITE, which converge
through ``get_or_create``. A callee leg owns an incoming call, a caller
leg the outgoing call of the user who dialed — the only record a call
placed from a native SIP phone ever gets, since no browser saw it.

A PBX payload always carries the conversation id and the browser
INVITE's Call-ID, so it matches on an exact key and never falls back to
the fuzzy number-and-recency match.

Execution order (visible in this function, not inferred transitive effects):

  1. Test self._is_inbound_external_leg(payload). If true:
    1. Return self.env['voip.call'].browse(); this branch ends here.
  2. Set user from self._get_user_from_pbx_call_event(payload).
  3. Test not user. If true:
    1. Test payload.get('user_uuid') or payload.get('dialed_extension'). If true:
      1. Evaluate _logger.warning('Ignoring PBX call event for conversation %s without Odoo softphone recipient', payload.get('conversation_id')); follow the named callee for its effects.
    2. Return self.env['voip.call'].browse(); this branch ends here.
  4. Set VoipCall from self.env['voip.call'].with_user(user).
  5. Set direction from self._get_direction_from_pbx_call_event(payload).
  6. Set phone_number from self._get_display_phone_number_from_pbx_call_event(payload).
  7. Set call_sudo from self.env['voip.call'].sudo().search([('conversation_id', '=', conversation.id), ('user_id', '=', user.id), ('direction', '=', direction), ('state', 'in', LIVE_CALL_STATES)], limit=1).
  8. Test not call_sudo. If true:
    1. Try these operations:
      1. Set call_data from VoipCall.get_or_create({'direction': direction, 'phone_number': phone_number, 'control_handle': payload['conversation_id'], 'sip_call_id': payload['sip_call_id'], 'skip_recent_pending_match': True}).

      On UniqueViolation:

      1. Raise ConcurrencyError(); follow the nearest applicable handler, not an assumed provider rollback.
    2. Set call_sudo from VoipCall.browse(call_data['ids'][0]).sudo().
  9. Set reclassified from payload.get('direction') == 'internal'.
  10. Test direction == 'incoming' and (not reclassified) and (call_sudo.state == 'calling') and (call_sudo.phone_number != phone_number). If true:
    1. Set call_sudo.phone_number from phone_number.
  11. Test not call_sudo.conversation_id. If true:
    1. Set call_sudo.conversation_id from conversation.
  12. Test not call_sudo.control_handle. If true:
    1. Set call_sudo.control_handle from payload['conversation_id'].
  13. Evaluate call_sudo._add_sip_call_id(payload['sip_call_id']); follow the named callee for its effects.
  14. Return call_sudo; this branch ends here.
VoipPhoneServiceEvent._ensure_leg

Inputs and defaults: VoipPhoneServiceEvent._ensure_leg(self, payload, conversation, call, event_type, occurred_at).

Decorators/execution contract: @api.model. Read decorator implementations: they can wrap, register or replace this function.

Maintainer's function contract:

Upsert the leg for this SIP Call-ID and stamp its lifecycle timing.

Reconciles onto a leg an earlier INVITE (browser stub) or webhook may
already have created, keyed by Call-ID then by ``(conversation, pbx_call_id)``,
so one physical leg never splits into two rows. Endpoint fields are
(re)resolved only on creation or on the rich ``call_created`` event, so
a timing-only answered/hangup stamp never clobbers them.

Execution order (visible in this function, not inferred transitive effects):

  1. Set Leg from self.env['voip.call.leg'].sudo().
  2. Set sip_call_id from payload.get('sip_call_id').
  3. Set pbx_call_id from payload.get('call_id').
  4. Set leg from Leg.search([('sip_call_id', '=', sip_call_id)], limit=1) if sip_call_id else Leg.browse().
  5. Test not leg and pbx_call_id. If true:
    1. Set leg from Leg.search([('conversation_id', '=', conversation.id), ('pbx_call_id', '=', pbx_call_id)], limit=1).
  6. Test not leg and (not pbx_call_id). If true:
    1. Return leg; this branch ends here.
  7. Set values from {'conversation_id': conversation.id}.
  8. Test event_type == 'call_created' or not leg. If true:
    1. Evaluate values.update(self._resolve_leg_endpoint(payload, conversation, call)); follow the named callee for its effects.

    Otherwise:

    1. Test call and (not leg.voip_call_id). If true:
      1. Set values['voip_call_id'] from call.id.
  9. Test pbx_call_id. If true:
    1. Set values['pbx_call_id'] from pbx_call_id.
  10. Test event_type == 'call_answered'. If true:
    1. Set values['answered_at'] from occurred_at.

    Otherwise:

    1. Test event_type == 'call_ended'. If true:
      1. Set values['ended_at'] from occurred_at.
  11. Test leg. If true:
    1. Evaluate leg.write(values); follow the named callee for its effects.
    2. Return leg; this branch ends here.
  12. Try these operations:
    1. Return Leg.create(values); this branch ends here.

    On UniqueViolation:

    1. Raise ConcurrencyError(); follow the nearest applicable handler, not an assumed provider rollback.
VoipPhoneServiceEvent._resolve_leg_endpoint

Inputs and defaults: VoipPhoneServiceEvent._resolve_leg_endpoint(self, payload, conversation, call=None).

Decorators/execution contract: @api.model. Read decorator implementations: they can wrap, register or replace this function.

Maintainer's function contract:

Resolve which endpoint this leg is, and which call it folds into.

A user's own caller leg is a "source" like the inbound trunk leg — both
are the endpoint that opened the conversation — and that is what keeps
``_is_answered_elsewhere`` and ``_is_answered_on_another_device``
correct: they read an answered *participant* leg as proof a device
picked up, and on an internal call the caller's leg lives in the same
conversation as the callee's. Unlike the trunk leg, it does fold into a
call: the outgoing call of the user who dialed.

Execution order (visible in this function, not inferred transitive effects):

  1. Set values from {'sip_call_id': payload.get('sip_call_id') or None}.
  2. Test self._is_inbound_external_leg(payload). If true:
    1. Set values['role'] from 'source'.
    2. Return values; this branch ends here.
  3. Test not (self._is_user_caller_leg(payload) or self._is_user_callee_leg(payload)). If true:
    1. Set values['role'] from 'routing'.
    2. Return values; this branch ends here.
  4. Set values['role'] from 'source' if self._is_user_caller_leg(payload) else 'participant'.
  5. Set target from call or self._find_user_call(payload, conversation).
  6. Test target. If true:
    1. Set values['voip_call_id'] from target.id.
  7. Return values; this branch ends here.
VoipPhoneServiceEvent._find_user_call

Inputs and defaults: VoipPhoneServiceEvent._find_user_call(self, payload, conversation).

Decorators/execution contract: @api.model. Read decorator implementations: they can wrap, register or replace this function.

Execution order (visible in this function, not inferred transitive effects):

  1. Set user from self.env['res.users']._get_from_pbx_user_uuid(payload['user_uuid']).
  2. Return self.env['voip.call'].sudo().search([('conversation_id', '=', conversation.id), ('user_id', '=', user.id), ('direction', '=', self._get_direction_from_pbx_call_event(payload))], limit=1); this branch ends here.
VoipPhoneServiceEvent._resolve_state_target

Inputs and defaults: VoipPhoneServiceEvent._resolve_state_target(self, payload, conversation, leg).

Decorators/execution contract: @api.model. Read decorator implementations: they can wrap, register or replace this function.

Maintainer's function contract:

Return the call(s) a state transition (answered/hangup) applies to.

A user leg drives its own call directly. The trunk/source leg owns no
call, so it drives the conversation's call only when it fans out to a
single softphone — never across a group/queue, where each member's own
leg carries its outcome.

Execution order (visible in this function, not inferred transitive effects):

  1. Test leg.voip_call_id. If true:
    1. Return leg.voip_call_id; this branch ends here.
  2. Test self._is_inbound_external_leg(payload) and len(conversation.call_ids) == 1. If true:
    1. Return conversation.call_ids; this branch ends here.
  3. Return self._find_call(payload.get('conversation_id'), payload.get('sip_call_id')); this branch ends here.
VoipPhoneServiceEvent._apply_answered

Inputs and defaults: VoipPhoneServiceEvent._apply_answered(self, calls, occurred_at).

Decorators/execution contract: @api.model. Read decorator implementations: they can wrap, register or replace this function.

Execution order (visible in this function, not inferred transitive effects):

  1. For each call in calls:
    1. Test call.state == 'ongoing'. If true:
      1. Execute continue.
    2. Test not call.start_call(at=occurred_at)['success']. If true:
      1. Execute continue.
    3. Evaluate call._notify_devices(); follow the named callee for its effects.
    4. Evaluate self._notify_call_update(call); follow the named callee for its effects.
    5. Test call.direction == 'incoming'. If true:
      1. Evaluate self._complete_ringing_peers(call); follow the named callee for its effects.
VoipPhoneServiceEvent._complete_ringing_peers

Inputs and defaults: VoipPhoneServiceEvent._complete_ringing_peers(self, call).

Decorators/execution contract: @api.model. Read decorator implementations: they can wrap, register or replace this function.

Maintainer's function contract:

Settle the other members of a group ring the moment one picks up.

Left to themselves, the losers each infer the winner's answer from a
concurrent transaction their snapshot cannot see, and a member reached
by push alone owns no PBX channel, so no later event ever corrects it:
that member settles "missed" and shows a missed-call notification for a
call a colleague took. The answering transaction is the one that holds
the fact, so it writes it to every peer instead.

A peer already settled "missed" by its own cancel racing this answer is
revised here — within one conversation there is one ring, so an answer
anywhere means no one else missed anything.

A peer still owing a hangup on its own PBX channel is left alone: that
event carries what the member actually did, and declining is its own
outcome that a colleague's answer must not overwrite.

Execution order (visible in this function, not inferred transitive effects):

  1. Test not call.conversation_id. If true:
    1. Return None; this branch ends here.
  2. Set peers from self.env['voip.call'].sudo().search([('conversation_id', '=', call.conversation_id.id), ('id', '!=', call.id), ('direction', '=', 'incoming'), ('state', 'in', ('calling', 'missed'))]).
  3. For each peer in peers:
    1. Test self._has_pending_pbx_leg(peer). If true:
      1. Execute continue.
    2. Set was_missed from peer.state == 'missed'.
    3. Test not peer.complete_call_elsewhere()['success']. If true:
      1. Execute continue.
    4. Evaluate peer._notify_devices(); follow the named callee for its effects.
    5. Evaluate self._notify_call_update(peer, with_missed_count=was_missed); follow the named callee for its effects.
VoipPhoneServiceEvent._apply_ended

Inputs and defaults: VoipPhoneServiceEvent._apply_ended(self, calls, payload, occurred_at, leg).

Decorators/execution contract: @api.model. Read decorator implementations: they can wrap, register or replace this function.

Execution order (visible in this function, not inferred transitive effects):

  1. Set disposition from self._hangup_disposition(payload).
  2. For each call in calls:
    1. Test call.state in TERMINAL_CALL_STATES. If true:
      1. Execute continue.
    2. Test disposition != 'answered' and self._is_answered_on_another_device(call, leg). If true:
      1. Execute continue.
    3. Test call.direction == 'outgoing'. If true:
      1. Evaluate self._end_outgoing_call(call, disposition, occurred_at); follow the named callee for its effects.

      Otherwise:

      1. Evaluate self._end_incoming_call(call, payload, disposition, occurred_at); follow the named callee for its effects.
    4. Evaluate call._notify_devices(); follow the named callee for its effects.
    5. Evaluate self._notify_call_update(call, with_missed_count=call.state == 'missed'); follow the named callee for its effects.
VoipPhoneServiceEvent._end_outgoing_call

Inputs and defaults: VoipPhoneServiceEvent._end_outgoing_call(self, call, disposition, occurred_at).

Decorators/execution contract: @api.model. Read decorator implementations: they can wrap, register or replace this function.

Maintainer's function contract:

Settle the call of the user who dialed.

A caller never "misses" their own call, and 'missed' is not even a legal
outgoing state: a callee who does not pick up aborts it, and a busy or
declined one rejects it. Asterisk propagates the far-end cause onto the
caller channel, so this leg's own reason code carries the callee's
verdict and the outbound trunk leg is never needed.

Execution order (visible in this function, not inferred transitive effects):

  1. Test call.state == 'ongoing' or disposition == 'answered'. If true:
    1. Evaluate call.end_call(at=occurred_at); follow the named callee for its effects.

    Otherwise:

    1. Test disposition in ('rejected', 'busy'). If true:
      1. Evaluate call.reject_call(); follow the named callee for its effects.

      Otherwise:

      1. Evaluate call.abort_call(); follow the named callee for its effects.
VoipPhoneServiceEvent._end_incoming_call

Inputs and defaults: VoipPhoneServiceEvent._end_incoming_call(self, call, payload, disposition, occurred_at).

Decorators/execution contract: @api.model. Read decorator implementations: they can wrap, register or replace this function.

Execution order (visible in this function, not inferred transitive effects):

  1. Test call.state == 'ongoing' or (disposition == 'answered' and (not self._is_inbound_external_leg(payload))). If true:
    1. Evaluate call.end_call(at=occurred_at); follow the named callee for its effects.

    Otherwise:

    1. Test disposition in ('rejected', 'busy'). If true:
      1. Evaluate call.reject_call(); follow the named callee for its effects.

      Otherwise:

      1. Test disposition == 'completed_elsewhere' or self._is_answered_elsewhere(call). If true:
        1. Evaluate call.complete_call_elsewhere(); follow the named callee for its effects.

        Otherwise:

        1. Evaluate call.miss_call(); follow the named callee for its effects.
VoipPhoneServiceEvent._hangup_disposition

Inputs and defaults: VoipPhoneServiceEvent._hangup_disposition(self, payload).

Decorators/execution contract: @api.model. Read decorator implementations: they can wrap, register or replace this function.

Execution order (visible in this function, not inferred transitive effects):

  1. Test payload['answer_time']. If true:
    1. Return 'answered'; this branch ends here.
  2. Return DISPOSITION_BY_HANGUP_CAUSE.get(payload['reason_code'], 'missed'); this branch ends here.
VoipPhoneServiceEvent._is_answered_on_another_device

Inputs and defaults: VoipPhoneServiceEvent._is_answered_on_another_device(self, call, leg).

Decorators/execution contract: @api.model. Read decorator implementations: they can wrap, register or replace this function.

Maintainer's function contract:

Whether the call's user picked up on another leg of the same call.

A user ringing on several devices gets one leg per device, all folded
into one call. When one device answers, Wazo clears the losing devices
with plain normal clearing (cause 16) an instant later: such a hangup
describes the losing device only, not the call, which lives on through
the answered leg. Role filters out the trunk source leg, which Wazo
answers itself (unbridged) to run no-answer fallbacks.

Execution order (visible in this function, not inferred transitive effects):

  1. Return bool(self.env['voip.call.leg'].sudo().search_count([('voip_call_id', '=', call.id), ('id', '!=', leg.id), ('role', '=', 'participant'), ('answered_at', '!=', False), ('ended_at', '=', False)], limit=1)); this branch ends here.
VoipPhoneServiceEvent._is_answered_elsewhere

Inputs and defaults: VoipPhoneServiceEvent._is_answered_elsewhere(self, call).

Decorators/execution contract: @api.model. Read decorator implementations: they can wrap, register or replace this function.

Maintainer's function contract:

Whether another member of the call's conversation picked up.

Wazo hangs up the losing members of a group ring with plain normal
clearing (cause 16), never answered-elsewhere (cause 26), so their
disposition reads "missed". The winner's answer is forwarded before the
losers' hangups: an answered participant leg on another call of the
same conversation is the signal that tells them apart. Role filters out
the trunk source leg, which Wazo answers itself (unbridged) to run
no-answer fallbacks.

Execution order (visible in this function, not inferred transitive effects):

ResPartner.get_contacts

Inputs and defaults: ResPartner.get_contacts(self, offset, limit, search_terms, internal_users_first=False, prioritized_contacts_limit=0).

Decorators/execution contract: @api.model. Read decorator implementations: they can wrap, register or replace this function.

Maintainer's function contract:

Fetch VoIP contacts matching the search and pagination parameters.

When ``prioritized_contacts_limit`` is non-zero, up to that many
matching contacts are selected by the VoIP call model and inserted
before the regular contact search results. The returned page is then
computed from that combined list, so ``offset`` and ``limit`` apply as
if prioritized contacts were the first rows of the result set. In that
mode, the response also includes all prioritized contact ids so the
client can keep the same ordering while filtering already-loaded
contacts locally. See ``_get_prioritized_contacts`` (e.g. getting
recently called partners first).

Execution order (visible in this function, not inferred transitive effects):

  1. Set domain from Domain('phone', '!=', False).
  2. Test search_terms. If true:
    1. Set escaped_search_terms from escape_like_value(search_terms).
    2. Set subdomain from Domain('complete_name', 'ilike', escaped_search_terms) | Domain('email', 'ilike', escaped_search_terms).
    3. Test len(search_terms) >= self._phone_search_min_length. If true:
      1. Execute subdomain |= Domain('phone_mobile_search', 'like', escaped_search_terms).
    4. Execute subdomain |= Domain('t9_name', 'ilike', f' {escaped_search_terms}').
    5. Execute domain &= subdomain.
  3. Set search_kwargs from {'offset': offset, 'limit': limit}.
  4. Test internal_users_first. If true:
    1. Set search_kwargs['order'] from f'partner_share ASC, {self._order}'.
  5. Test not prioritized_contacts_limit. If true:
    1. Set contacts from self.search(domain, **search_kwargs).
    2. Return Store().add(contacts, '_store_voip_fields'); this branch ends here.
  6. Set prioritized_contacts from self.env['voip.call']._get_prioritized_contacts(domain, limit=prioritized_contacts_limit).
  7. Test prioritized_contacts. If true:
    1. Execute domain &= Domain('id', 'not in', prioritized_contacts.ids).
  8. Test offset < len(prioritized_contacts). If true:
    1. Set prioritized_contacts_page from prioritized_contacts[offset:offset + limit].
    2. Set search_kwargs['offset'] from 0.
    3. Set search_kwargs['limit'] from limit - len(prioritized_contacts_page).

    Otherwise:

    1. Set prioritized_contacts_page from self.env['res.partner'].
    2. Set search_kwargs['offset'] from offset - len(prioritized_contacts).
  9. Set contacts from self.search(domain, **search_kwargs) if search_kwargs['limit'] else self.env['res.partner'].
  10. Return {'store_data': Store().add(prioritized_contacts_page | contacts, '_store_voip_fields'), 'prioritized_contact_ids': prioritized_contacts.ids}; this branch ends here.

Inputs and defaults: ResUsers._prepare_pbx_user_settings(self).

Execution order (visible in this function, not inferred transitive effects):

  1. Evaluate self.ensure_one(); follow the named callee for its effects.
  2. Set settings from self.env['res.users.settings'].sudo()._find_or_create_for_user(self).
  3. Set vals from {}.
  4. Test not settings.voip_secret. If true:
    1. Set vals['voip_secret'] from secrets.token_urlsafe(24).
  5. Test not settings.voip_busy_destination_type. If true:
    1. Set vals['voip_busy_destination_type'] from 'none'.
  6. Test not settings.voip_disconnected_destination_type. If true:

  7. Set phone from self.partner_id.phone and self.partner_id._phone_format(number=self.partner_id.phone, country=self.partner_id.country_id).
  8. Set has_valid_phone from phone and E164_NUMBER_RE.fullmatch(phone).
  9. Test not settings.voip_no_answer_destination_type. If true:
    1. Test not settings.voip_no_answer_timeout. If true:

    2. Test has_valid_phone. If true:
      1. Evaluate vals.update({'voip_no_answer_destination_type': 'forward', 'voip_no_answer_destination_kind': 'external', 'voip_no_answer_outcall_number': phone}); follow the named callee for its effects.
  10. Test vals. If true:
    1. Set should_notify_config from bool(VOIP_CONFIG_FIELDS & vals.keys()).
    2. Evaluate settings.with_context(voip_skip_config_bus=True, voip_skip_pbx_sync=True).write(vals); follow the named callee for its effects.
    3. Test should_notify_config and (not self.env.context.get('voip_skip_config_bus')). If true:

  11. Return settings; this branch ends here.

    2. Try these operations:
      1. Set data from service._ensure_wakeup_tokens(payload).

      On UserError:

      1. Evaluate _logger.warning('Wakeup-token reconcile batch failed: %s', error); follow the named callee for its effects.
      2. Execute continue.
    3. Evaluate failed.extend((uid for uid, ok in (data.get('results') or {}).items() if not ok)); follow the named callee for its effects.
  5. Test failed. If true:
    1. Evaluate _logger.warning('Wakeup-token reconcile could not settle %d user(s): %s', len(failed), ', '.join(sorted(failed))); follow the named callee for its effects.

ResUsers._reflect_change_in_res_users_settings

Inputs and defaults: ResUsers._reflect_change_in_res_users_settings(self).

Maintainer's function contract:

Updates the values of the VoIP User Configuration Fields in `res_users_settings_ids` to have the same values as
their related fields in `res.users`. If there is no `res.users.settings` record for the user, then the record is
created.

This method is intended to be used as an inverse for VoIP Configuration Fields.

Execution order (visible in this function, not inferred transitive effects):

  1. Set notify_voip_config_users from self.env['res.users'].
  2. For each user in self:
    1. Set settings from self.env['res.users.settings']._find_or_create_for_user(user).
    2. Set configuration from {field: user[field] for field in self._get_voip_user_configuration_fields()}.
    3. Set configuration['how_to_call_on_mobile'] from user.how_to_call_on_mobile or settings.how_to_call_on_mobile.
    4. Set pbx_sync_fields from {field_name for field_name in PBX_SYNC_FIELDS if settings[field_name] != user[field_name]}.
    5. Set sync_odoo_extension from not self.env.context.get('voip_skip_pbx_sync') and user.voip_provider_id == self.env['voip.pbx.service'].voip_provider and (settings.voip_provider_id != user.voip_provider_id).
    6. Set voip_config_changed from any((settings[field_name] != user[field_name] for field_name in VOIP_CONFIG_FIELDS)).
    7. Test voip_config_changed. If true:
      1. Execute notify_voip_config_users |= user.
    8. Evaluate settings.with_context(voip_skip_config_bus=True, voip_skip_pbx_sync=True).update(configuration); follow the named callee for its effects.
    9. Test sync_odoo_extension. If true:
      1. Evaluate settings._sync_odoo_extension(); follow the named callee for its effects.
    10. Test pbx_sync_fields and (not self.env.context.get('voip_skip_pbx_sync')). If true:
      1. Evaluate settings._voip_sync_pbx(); follow the named callee for its effects.
  3. Test notify_voip_config_users. If true:
    1. Evaluate notify_voip_config_users._bus_send('voip.config/updated', {}); follow the named callee for its effects.

    2. Test call.duration < 60. If true:
      1. Set call.duration_human_readable from self.env._('%(seconds)ss', seconds=call.duration).
      2. Execute continue.
    3. Set (minutes, seconds) from divmod(call.duration, 60).
    4. Test minutes < 60. If true:
      1. Set call.duration_human_readable from self.env._('%(minutes)sm %(seconds)ss', minutes=minutes, seconds=seconds).
      2. Execute continue.
    5. Set (hours, minutes) from divmod(minutes, 60).
    6. Set call.duration_human_readable from self.env._('%(hours)sh %(minutes)sm %(seconds)ss', hours=hours, minutes=minutes, seconds=seconds).

VoipCall._add_sip_call_id

Inputs and defaults: VoipCall._add_sip_call_id(self, sip_call_id).

Maintainer's function contract:

Attach a SIP Call-ID to this call by materializing its leg.

Wazo emits one leg per SIP Call-ID; all legs of a queue conversation
share ``control_handle`` but carry distinct Call-IDs. Each Call-ID
lives on its own ``voip.call.leg`` so the browser can match the
notification action with whichever INVITE reached that tab or device.
The leg is found-or-created: a webhook may already have materialized it
(keyed by PBX call id), in which case we only bind it to this call.

Execution order (visible in this function, not inferred transitive effects):

  1. Test not sip_call_id. If true:
    1. Return None; this branch ends here.
  2. Set Leg from self.env['voip.call.leg'].sudo().
  3. For each call in self:
    1. Set leg from Leg.search([('sip_call_id', '=', sip_call_id)], limit=1).
    2. Test leg. If true:
      1. Test not leg.voip_call_id. If true:
        1. Set leg.voip_call_id from call.

      Otherwise:

      1. Try these operations:
        1. Evaluate Leg.create({'voip_call_id': call.id, 'conversation_id': call.conversation_id.id, 'sip_call_id': sip_call_id}); follow the named callee for its effects.

        On UniqueViolation:

        1. Raise ConcurrencyError(); follow the nearest applicable handler, not an assumed provider rollback.
VoipCall._find_by_sip_call_id

Inputs and defaults: VoipCall._find_by_sip_call_id(self, sip_call_id, direction='incoming').

Maintainer's function contract:

Return the call whose leg tracks ``sip_call_id``, in ``direction``.

Scoped to the current environment user so an INVITE from one user cannot
attach itself to another user's call record. Outgoing calls are looked
up the same way: the browser sends its INVITE's Call-ID, which is what
the PBX reports as ``sip_call_id`` on that same leg, so a browser call
and its webhooks converge on one record whichever arrives first.

Execution order (visible in this function, not inferred transitive effects):

  1. Test not sip_call_id. If true:
    1. Return self.browse(); this branch ends here.
  2. Set leg from self.env['voip.call.leg'].sudo().search([('sip_call_id', '=', sip_call_id), ('voip_call_id.direction', '=', direction), ('voip_call_id.user_id', '=', self.env.uid)], limit=1).
  3. Return self.browse(leg.voip_call_id.id) if leg.voip_call_id else self.browse(); this branch ends here.
VoipCall._find_incoming_by_sip_call_id

Inputs and defaults: VoipCall._find_incoming_by_sip_call_id(self, sip_call_id).

Decorators/execution contract: @api.model. Read decorator implementations: they can wrap, register or replace this function.

Maintainer's function contract:

Webhook-side variant of ``_find_by_sip_call_id``: PBX push events
carry no Odoo user context, so the lookup spans all users.

Execution order (visible in this function, not inferred transitive effects):

  1. Test not sip_call_id. If true:
    1. Return self.sudo().browse(); this branch ends here.
  2. Set leg from self.env['voip.call.leg'].sudo().search([('sip_call_id', '=', sip_call_id), ('voip_call_id.direction', '=', 'incoming')], order='id desc', limit=1).
  3. Return leg.voip_call_id.sudo(); this branch ends here.
VoipCall._find_recent_pending_incoming_call

Inputs and defaults: VoipCall._find_recent_pending_incoming_call(self, phone_number).

Maintainer's function contract:

Return the webhook-created call while Wazo has not sent the browser leg yet.

Wazo may first send a source-leg webhook, then deliver the browser INVITE
with a different SIP Call-ID, and only later send the callee-leg webhook
that carries this second SIP Call-ID. During that short race window the
INVITE must attach to the already-notified call instead of creating a
duplicate.

Execution order (visible in this function, not inferred transitive effects):

  1. Set phone_numbers from [phone_number] if phone_number else [].
  2. Set user from self.env['res.users.settings']._get_user_from_voip_username(phone_number).
  3. Test user.routing_extension_id.number. If true:
    1. Evaluate phone_numbers.append(user.routing_extension_id.number); follow the named callee for its effects.
  4. Set phone_numbers from list(dict.fromkeys(phone_numbers)).
  5. Test not phone_numbers. If true:
    1. Return self.browse(); this branch ends here.
  6. Set candidates from self.sudo().search([('user_id', '=', self.env.uid), ('direction', '=', 'incoming'), ('state', '=', 'calling'), ('create_date', '>=', fields.Datetime.now() - timedelta(minutes=2))], order='id desc').
  7. For each call in candidates:
    1. Test any((same_number(call.phone_number, number) for number in phone_numbers)). If true:
      1. Return call.sudo(False); this branch ends here.
  8. Return self.browse(); this branch ends here.

  2. Set context from {'default_activity_category': 'phonecall', 'default_activity_type_id': self.env.ref('mail.mail_activity_data_call').id, 'default_call_id': self.id, 'default_date_deadline': False, 'default_res_model_selection': 'res.partner', 'voip_log_contact_id': self.par….
  3. Test active_model and active_id. If true:
    1. Evaluate context.update(self._get_field_selection_for_model(active_model, active_id) or {}); follow the named callee for its effects.
  4. Return {'name': self.env._('Log Activity in Chatter'), 'type': 'ir.actions.act_window', 'res_model': 'mail.activity.schedule', 'view_mode': 'form', 'views': [(self.env.ref('voip.voip_activity_schedule_form_view').id, 'form')], 'target': 'new', 'context': context}; this branch ends here.
VoipCall._get_field_selection_for_model

Inputs and defaults: VoipCall._get_field_selection_for_model(self, model_name, id).

Maintainer's function contract:

Find the res_model_selection option matching the given model and
return the context dict to pre-fill the wizard.

:return: A dict like ``{"default_lead_id": id}``, or ``None``.

Execution order (visible in this function, not inferred transitive effects):

  1. Test model_name == 'res.partner'. If true:
    1. Return None; this branch ends here.
  2. Set wizard from self.env['mail.activity.schedule'].with_context(voip_log_contact_id=self.partner_id.id).new({'call_id': self.id}).
  3. Set fields_map from wizard._get_res_model_fields().
  4. For each (value, _label) in wizard._selection_res_model():
    1. Test wizard._get_res_model_from_selection(value) != model_name. If true:
      1. Execute continue.
    2. Set field_name from fields_map.get(value).
    3. Set domain_field from f'{field_name}_domain'.
    4. Test domain_field in wizard._fields. If true:
      1. Set domain_str from wizard[domain_field] or '[]'.
      2. Set domain from ast.literal_eval(domain_str).
      3. Test not self.env[model_name].search_count(Domain('id', '=', id) & Domain(domain), limit=1). If true:
        1. Execute continue.
    5. Return {f'default_{field_name}': id, 'default_res_model_selection': value}; this branch ends here.
  5. Return None; this branch ends here.

VoipCall.get_prefill_data

Inputs and defaults: VoipCall.get_prefill_data(self, res_model, res_id).

Decorators/execution contract: @api.model. Read decorator implementations: they can wrap, register or replace this function.

Maintainer's function contract:

Get the partner phone and store data for keypad pre-filling from a
form view, so the softphone can auto-fill the dialer and display the
partner in the contact suggestions.

Falls back to the record's own phone fields (via ``_phone_get_number_fields``)
when no linked partner is found or the partner has no phone number.

:param str res_model: model name of the record
:param int res_id: ID of the record
:returns: dict with ``partner_id``, ``phone`` and ``store_data``, or an empty dict

Execution order (visible in this function, not inferred transitive effects):

  1. Set record from self.env[res_model].browse(res_id).
  2. Test not record.exists() or not record.has_access('read'). If true:
    1. Return {}; this branch ends here.
  3. Set store from Store().
  4. Set partners from record._mail_get_partners(introspect_fields=True).get(record.id).
  5. Set partner from partners[:1].
  6. Test partner. If true:
    1. Evaluate store.add(partner, '_store_voip_fields'); follow the named callee for its effects.
  7. Set phone from partner.phone_formatted or partner.phone_sanitized or partner.phone or record._phone_format().
  8. Test phone. If true:
    1. Return {'partner_id': partner.id, 'phone': phone, 'store_data': store}; this branch ends here.
  9. Return {}; this branch ends here.
VoipCall.get_or_create

Inputs and defaults: VoipCall.get_or_create(self, data).

Decorators/execution contract: @api.model. Read decorator implementations: they can wrap, register or replace this function.

Maintainer's function contract:

Return the matching call record for an incoming SIP INVITE.

Wazo webhooks and browser INVITEs can arrive in either order and can
carry different SIP Call-IDs for the same conversation. They are
correlated through the control handle, then the SIP Call-ID header
(webhook ``sip_call_id`` == INVITE ``Call-ID``), then the short
pending-call fallback.

The control handle is the PBX conversation id
(``X-Odoo-Conversation-Id`` header) for the Odoo provider, the only
one trusted to stamp that header, and the INVITE Call-ID for every
other provider.

The control handle match only considers live calls: a record in a
terminal state is frozen history, so a later INVITE reusing the same
conversation id (queue retry, transfer or park recall) starts a new
call record instead of resurrecting the old one.

Execution order (visible in this function, not inferred transitive effects):

  1. Evaluate self.check_access('read'); follow the named callee for its effects.
  2. Set skip_recent_pending_match from data.pop('skip_recent_pending_match', False).
  3. Set control_handle from data.get('control_handle').
  4. Set sip_call_id from data.pop('sip_call_id', None).
  5. Set direction from data.get('direction').
  6. Test direction == 'incoming' and control_handle == sip_call_id and self.env.user.uses_odoo_provider. If true:
    1. Evaluate _logger.warning('INVITE %s reached the softphone without X-Odoo-Conversation-Id; call of user %s cannot be correlated with its PBX conversation.', sip_call_id, self.env.uid); follow the named callee for its effects.
  7. Set call from self.env['voip.call'].
  8. Test control_handle. If true:
    1. Set call from self.env['voip.call'].sudo().search([('control_handle', '=', control_handle), ('user_id', '=', self.env.uid), ('direction', '=', direction), ('state', 'in', LIVE_CALL_STATES)], limit=1).
  9. Test not call. If true:
    1. Set call from self._find_by_sip_call_id(sip_call_id or control_handle, direction).
  10. Test not call and direction == 'incoming' and (not skip_recent_pending_match). If true:
    1. Set call from self._find_recent_pending_incoming_call(data.get('phone_number')).
  11. Test call. If true:
    1. Set call from call.sudo(False).
    2. Evaluate call._add_sip_call_id(sip_call_id); follow the named callee for its effects.
    3. Evaluate call._sync_has_active_call(); follow the named callee for its effects.
    4. Set outcome from 'matched'.
    5. Set result from {'ids': [call.id], 'store_data': call._get_store_data()}.

    Otherwise:

    1. Set outcome from 'created'.
    2. Try these operations:
      1. Set result from self.create_and_format(**data).

      On UniqueViolation:

      1. Raise ConcurrencyError(); follow the nearest applicable handler, not an assumed provider rollback.
    3. Test sip_call_id. If true:
      1. Evaluate self.browse(result['ids'][0])._add_sip_call_id(sip_call_id); follow the named callee for its effects.
  12. Evaluate _logger.info('get_or_create user=%s %s %s control_handle=%s sip_call_id=%s -> %s call %s', self.env.uid, direction, data.get('phone_number'), control_handle, sip_call_id, outcome, result['ids'][0]); follow the named callee for its effects.
  13. Return result; this branch ends here.
VoipCall.create_and_format

Inputs and defaults: VoipCall.create_and_format(self, phone_number: str, direction: str='outgoing', partner_id: int | None=None, activity_id: int | None=None, control_handle: str | None=None, res_id: int | None=None, res_model: str | None=None, is_production: bool=True).

Decorators/execution contract: @api.model. Read decorator implementations: they can wrap, register or replace this function.

Maintainer's function contract:

Creates a call from the provided values and returns it formatted for
use in JavaScript. If a record is provided via its id and model,
introspects it for a recipient.

:param phone_number: Phone number of the remote party
:param direction: Call direction
:param partner_id: Optional partner linked to the call
:param activity_id: Optional phone activity linked to the call
:param control_handle: Optional provider-side call handle
:param res_id: Optional record ID to extract partner from
:param res_model: Optional model name to extract partner from
:param is_production: Whether this call is happening in a production environment.

Returns:
    Dictionary with created call IDs and formatted data

Execution order (visible in this function, not inferred transitive effects):

  1. Evaluate self.check_access('read'); follow the named callee for its effects.
  2. Test activity_id. If true:
    1. Evaluate self.env['mail.activity'].browse(activity_id).check_access('read'); follow the named callee for its effects.
  3. Test direction == 'incoming'. If true:
    1. Set phone_number from self._resolve_incoming_caller_number(phone_number).
  4. Set values from {'activity_id': activity_id, 'control_handle': control_handle, 'direction': direction, 'partner_id': partner_id, 'phone_number': phone_number, 'user_id': self.env.uid, 'is_production': is_production}.
  5. Test res_id and res_model and (related_record := self.env[res_model].browse(res_id)).exists(). If true:
    1. Evaluate related_record.check_access('read'); follow the named callee for its effects.
    2. Set values['partner_id'] from next(iter(related_record._mail_get_partners(introspect_fields=True)[related_record.id]), self.env['res.partner']).id.
    3. Test not activity_id. If true:
      1. Try these operations:
        1. Enter context self.env.cr.savepoint(); its exit semantics matter:
          1. Set values['activity_id'] from self._create_call_activity(related_record).id.

        On PG_CONCURRENCY_EXCEPTIONS_TO_RETRY:

        1. Raise the current exception; follow the nearest applicable handler, not an assumed provider rollback.

        On Exception:

        1. Evaluate _logger.warning('Failed to create call activity for %s/%s', res_model, res_id, exc_info=True); follow the named callee for its effects.
  6. Set call from self.sudo().create(values).sudo(False).
  7. Set store from Store().add(call, '_store_voip_fields').
  8. Return {'ids': [call.id], 'store_data': store}; this branch ends here.

Inputs and defaults: VoipCall.resolve_outgoing_dial_number(self, number).

Decorators/execution contract: @api.model. Read decorator implementations: they can wrap, register or replace this function.

Maintainer's function contract:

Resolve the PBX target and report whether it stays inside the tenant.

Execution order (visible in this function, not inferred transitive effects):

  1. Evaluate self.check_access('read'); follow the named callee for its effects.
  2. Set did from self.env['voip.did.number']._get_from_number(number).
  3. Test did.destination_ref. If true:
    1. Test did.destination_ref._name == 'voip.extension'. If true:

        Otherwise:

        1. Set extension from self.env['voip.extension'].
    2. Test extension.number. If true:
      1. Return {'number': extension.number, 'is_internal': True}; this branch ends here.
  4. Set extension from self.env['voip.extension'].sudo().search([('number', '=', number)], limit=1).
  5. Return {'number': number, 'is_internal': bool(extension or re.fullmatch('\\*\\d+', number or ''))}; this branch ends here.

VoipCall._decline_via_pbx

Inputs and defaults: VoipCall._decline_via_pbx(self).

Maintainer's function contract:

Decline this incoming call in the PBX, for this member alone.

Hangs up the member's own ringing legs. A push-only member has none, and
the push names no leg of theirs — on a direct call it names the caller's
— so the PBX resolves the ring leg from the conversation and the user.

Execution order (visible in this function, not inferred transitive effects):

  1. Evaluate self.ensure_one(); follow the named callee for its effects.
  2. Evaluate self.check_access('read'); follow the named callee for its effects.
  3. Set call_sudo from self.sudo().
  4. Set api from PhoneServiceAPI(call_sudo.env).
  5. Set handles from [leg.pbx_call_id for leg in call_sudo.leg_ids if leg.pbx_call_id and (not leg.ended_at)].
  6. Test handles. If true:
    1. For each call_id in handles:
      1. Evaluate api.hangup_call(call_id); follow the named callee for its effects.

    Otherwise:

    1. Test call_sudo.conversation_id and call_sudo.user_id.voip_pbx_user_uuid. If true:
      1. Evaluate api.decline_call(call_sudo.conversation_id.conversation_identifier, call_sudo.user_id.voip_pbx_user_uuid); follow the named callee for its effects.

Inputs and defaults: VoipCall._sync_has_active_call(self, excluded_call_ids=None, users=None).

Synchronizes ``has_active_call`` for users linked to calls.

    1. Set has_active_call from user in active_users.
    2. Test user.has_active_call == has_active_call. If true:

    3. Set user.sudo().has_active_call from has_active_call.
    4. Evaluate stores[user, 'presence'].add(user, '_store_has_active_call_fields'); follow the named callee for its effects.

  10. Test len(matches) <= 1. If true:
    1. Return matches; this branch ends here.
  11. Set best from min(matches, key=self._timing_distance).
  12. Evaluate _logger.warning('call_cost %s matches %s calls to %s in window; attaching to closest call %s', self.event_id, len(matches), number, best.id); follow the named callee for its effects.

Project graph_data onto what PBX sync cares about, ignoring canvas layout.

Moving or resizing a node on the canvas must not trigger a PBX resync: it
changes nothing about routing, so `position`/`size` are stripped before

Execution order (visible in this function, not inferred transitive effects):

  1. Evaluate self.ensure_one(); follow the named callee for its effects.

    1. Return graph_data; this branch ends here.
  5. Set nodes_by_id from {node.get('id'): {key: value for key, value in node.items() if key not in GRAPH_LAYOUT_NODE_KEYS} for node in nodes if isinstance(node, dict)}.
  6. Return (nodes_by_id, graph_data.get('connections')); this branch ends here.

Validate complete graphs before triggering any external PBX effect.

Execution order (visible in this function, not inferred transitive effects):

VoipCallFlow._validate_graph_data

Inputs and defaults: VoipCallFlow._validate_graph_data(self).

Maintainer's function contract:

Validate graph structure, record references and Time Condition placement.

Execution order (visible in this function, not inferred transitive effects):

  1. Evaluate self.ensure_one(); follow the named callee for its effects.
  2. Set graph_data from self.graph_data.
  3. Test not isinstance(graph_data, dict). If true:
    1. Raise ValidationError(self.env._('The Call Flow graph must be an object.')); follow the nearest applicable handler, not an assumed provider rollback.
  4. Set nodes from graph_data.get('nodes').
  5. Set connections from graph_data.get('connections').
  6. Test not isinstance(nodes, list) or not isinstance(connections, list). If true:
    1. Raise ValidationError(self.env._('The Call Flow graph must contain nodes and connections.')); follow the nearest applicable handler, not an assumed provider rollback.
  7. Set nodes_by_id from {}.
  8. Set records_by_model from {model_name: self.env[model_name] for model_name in CALL_FLOW_OUTPUT_NODE_MODELS.values()}.
  9. For each node in nodes:
    1. Test not isinstance(node, dict) or not isinstance(node.get('id'), (int, str)) or isinstance(node.get('id'), bool). If true:
      1. Raise ValidationError(self.env._('Every Call Flow node must have a valid ID.')); follow the nearest applicable handler, not an assumed provider rollback.
    2. Set node_id from node['id'].
    3. Test node_id in nodes_by_id. If true:
      1. Raise ValidationError(self.env._('Call Flow node IDs must be unique.')); follow the nearest applicable handler, not an assumed provider rollback.
    4. Set nodes_by_id[node_id] from node.
    5. Set node_type from node.get('type').
    6. Test node_type not in (*CALL_FLOW_RECORD_NODE_MODELS, 'hangup', 'outcall', 'start'). If true:
      1. Raise ValidationError(self.env._('The Call Flow contains an unsupported node.')); follow the nearest applicable handler, not an assumed provider rollback.
    7. Test not isinstance(node.get('outputs'), list). If true:
      1. Raise ValidationError(self.env._('Every Call Flow node must define its outputs.')); follow the nearest applicable handler, not an assumed provider rollback.
    8. Set output_ids from [output.get('id') for output in node['outputs'] if isinstance(output, dict) and isinstance(output.get('id'), (int, str)) and (output.get('direction') == 'output')].
    9. Test len(output_ids) != len(node['outputs']) or len(output_ids) != len(set(output_ids)). If true:
      1. Raise ValidationError(self.env._('A Call Flow node has invalid output ports.')); follow the nearest applicable handler, not an assumed provider rollback.
    10. Set expected_model from CALL_FLOW_RECORD_NODE_MODELS.get(node_type).
    11. Test expected_model. If true:
      1. Set record_data from node.get('record').
      2. Test not isinstance(record_data, dict) or record_data.get('resModel') != expected_model or (not isinstance(record_data.get('resId'), int)). If true:
        1. Raise ValidationError(self.env._('The %(node_type)s node has an invalid destination.', node_type=node_type)); follow the nearest applicable handler, not an assumed provider rollback.
      3. Set record from self.env[expected_model].browse(record_data['resId']).exists().
      4. Test not record. If true:
        1. Raise ValidationError(self.env._('A destination used by the Call Flow no longer exists.')); follow the nearest applicable handler, not an assumed provider rollback.
      5. Test expected_model in records_by_model. If true:
        1. Test record in records_by_model[expected_model]. If true:
          1. Raise ValidationError(self.env._('%(record_name)s cannot be used more than once in the same Call Flow.', record_name=record.display_name)); follow the nearest applicable handler, not an assumed provider rollback.
        2. Execute records_by_model[expected_model] |= record.
  10. Set start_nodes from [node for node in nodes if node['type'] == 'start'].
  11. Test len(start_nodes) != 1. If true:
    1. Raise ValidationError(self.env._('The Call Flow must contain exactly one Start node.')); follow the nearest applicable handler, not an assumed provider rollback.
  12. Test start_nodes[0].get('input') or [output['id'] for output in start_nodes[0]['outputs']] != ['next']. If true:
    1. Raise ValidationError(self.env._('The Start node must have exactly one output and no input.')); follow the nearest applicable handler, not an assumed provider rollback.
  13. Set seen_connections from set().
  14. Set connection_counts from {}.
  15. For each connection in connections:
    1. Test not isinstance(connection, dict). If true:
      1. Raise ValidationError(self.env._('The Call Flow contains an invalid connection.')); follow the nearest applicable handler, not an assumed provider rollback.
    2. Set source from nodes_by_id.get(connection.get('sourceNodeId')).
    3. Set target from nodes_by_id.get(connection.get('targetNodeId')).
    4. Test not source or not target. If true:
      1. Raise ValidationError(self.env._('The Call Flow contains an invalid connection.')); follow the nearest applicable handler, not an assumed provider rollback.
    5. Set source_port_id from connection.get('sourcePortId').
    6. Set target_port_id from connection.get('targetPortId').
    7. Set source_port from next((output for output in source['outputs'] if output['id'] == source_port_id), None).
    8. Set target_port from target.get('input').
    9. Test not isinstance(target_port, dict) or target_port.get('direction') != 'input'. If true:
      1. Set target_port from None.
    10. Test not source_port or not target_port or target_port.get('id') != target_port_id. If true:
      1. Raise ValidationError(self.env._('A Call Flow connection uses an invalid port.')); follow the nearest applicable handler, not an assumed provider rollback.
    11. Test target_port.get('accepts') is not None and source_port.get('provides') not in target_port['accepts']. If true:
      1. Raise ValidationError(self.env._('A Call Flow connection uses incompatible ports.')); follow the nearest applicable handler, not an assumed provider rollback.
    12. Set connection_key from (source['id'], source_port_id, target['id'], target_port_id).
    13. Test connection_key in seen_connections. If true:
      1. Raise ValidationError(self.env._('The Call Flow contains a duplicate connection.')); follow the nearest applicable handler, not an assumed provider rollback.
    14. Evaluate seen_connections.add(connection_key); follow the named callee for its effects.
    15. For each (port_key, port) in ((('source', source['id'], source_port_id), source_port), (('target', target['id'], target_port_id), target_port)):
      1. Set connection_counts[port_key] from connection_counts.get(port_key, 0) + 1.
      2. Test port.get('maxConnections') is not None and connection_counts[port_key] > port['maxConnections']. If true:
        1. Raise ValidationError(self.env._('A Call Flow connection uses a saturated port.')); follow the nearest applicable handler, not an assumed provider rollback.
  16. Set time_condition_nodes from [node for node in nodes if isinstance(node, dict) and node.get('type') == 'time_condition'].
  17. Set start_target from self._get_graph_output_nodes(start_nodes[0], ('next',), nodes_by_id, connections)['next'].
  18. Set connected_node_ids from {connection['targetNodeId'] for connection in connections}.
  19. Set claimed_owner_node_ids from set().
  20. For each node in time_condition_nodes:
    1. Test [output['id'] for output in node['outputs']] != ['open', 'closed']. If true:
      1. Raise ValidationError(self.env._('A Time Condition node must have one Open and one Closed output.')); follow the nearest applicable handler, not an assumed provider rollback.
    2. Test node == start_target. If true:
      1. Execute continue.
    3. Set open_target from self._get_graph_output_nodes(node, ('open',), nodes_by_id, connections)['open'].
    4. Test not open_target or open_target.get('type') not in ('call_group', 'queue'). If true:
      1. Test node['id'] not in connected_node_ids. If true:
        1. Execute continue.
      2. Raise ValidationError(self.env._('A Time Condition outside Start must have its Open output connected to a Call Group or Queue.')); follow the nearest applicable handler, not an assumed provider rollback.
    5. Test open_target['id'] in claimed_owner_node_ids. If true:
      1. Raise ValidationError(self.env._('A Call Group or Queue cannot use more than one Time Condition.')); follow the nearest applicable handler, not an assumed provider rollback.
    6. Evaluate claimed_owner_node_ids.add(open_target['id']); follow the named callee for its effects.
  21. Return records_by_model; this branch ends here.
VoipCallFlow._sync_graph_memberships

Inputs and defaults: VoipCallFlow._sync_graph_memberships(self).

Maintainer's function contract:

Assign output-bearing PBX records exclusively to their Call Flow.

Execution order (visible in this function, not inferred transitive effects):

  1. Set records_by_call_flow from {}.
  2. Set owners_by_record from {}.
  3. For each call_flow in self:
    1. Set records_by_call_flow[call_flow] from call_flow._get_graph_output_records().
    2. For each records in records_by_call_flow[call_flow].values():
      1. For each record in records:
        1. Set record_key from (record._name, record.id).
        2. Test record_key in owners_by_record. If true:
          1. Raise ValidationError(self.env._('%(record_name)s cannot be used more than once in Call Flows.', record_name=record.display_name)); follow the nearest applicable handler, not an assumed provider rollback.
        3. Set owners_by_record[record_key] from call_flow.
        4. Test record.callflow_id and record.callflow_id != call_flow. If true:
          1. Raise ValidationError(self.env._('%(record_name)s is already used in the Call Flow %(call_flow_name)s.', record_name=record.display_name, call_flow_name=record.callflow_id.display_name)); follow the nearest applicable handler, not an assumed provider rollback.
  4. Set sync_context from {'voip_call_flow_sync': True}.
  5. For each model_name in CALL_FLOW_OUTPUT_NODE_MODELS.values():
    1. Set assigned_records from self.env[model_name].search([('callflow_id', 'in', self.ids)]).
    2. Set desired_records from self.env[model_name].
    3. For each (call_flow, records_by_model) in records_by_call_flow.items():
      1. Set records from records_by_model[model_name].
      2. Execute desired_records |= records.
      3. Set records.filtered(lambda record: record.callflow_id != call_flow).with_context(**sync_context).callflow_id from call_flow.
    4. Set released_records from assigned_records - desired_records.
    5. Evaluate self._release_output_owning_records(released_records, CALL_FLOW_OUTPUT_FIELDS[model_name]); follow the named callee for its effects.
VoipCallFlow._release_output_owning_records

Inputs and defaults: VoipCallFlow._release_output_owning_records(self, records, output_fields).

Maintainer's function contract:

Clear Call Flow membership and PBX destinations on released records.

IVRs need their options' destinations cleared too and an explicit
PBX resync, unlike Call Group/Queue whose own write() already
triggers it.

Execution order (visible in this function, not inferred transitive effects):

  1. Test not records. If true:
    1. Return None; this branch ends here.
  2. Set sync_context from {'voip_call_flow_sync': True}.
  3. Test records._name == 'voip.ivr'. If true:
    1. Evaluate records.with_context(**sync_context, voip_skip_pbx_sync=True).write({'callflow_id': False, **dict.fromkeys(output_fields, False)}); follow the named callee for its effects.
    2. Evaluate records.option_ids.with_context(**sync_context, voip_skip_pbx_sync=True).write({'destination_ref': False}); follow the named callee for its effects.
    3. Evaluate records._sync_pbx(); follow the named callee for its effects.

    Otherwise:

    1. Test records._name == 'voip.time.condition'. If true:
      1. Evaluate records._release_from_call_flow(); follow the named callee for its effects.

      Otherwise:

      1. Evaluate records.with_context(**sync_context).write({'callflow_id': False, **dict.fromkeys(output_fields, False)}); follow the named callee for its effects.

Store both Time Condition branches and synchronize them with Wazo.

  1. For each call_flow in self:

        1. Evaluate call_flow._sync_time_condition_owner_schedule(previous_queue, None); follow the named callee for its effects.
      12. Evaluate time_condition._sync_pbx(); follow the named callee for its effects.

  10. Test not start_connections. If true:

VoipDidNumber.write

Inputs and defaults: VoipDidNumber.write(self, vals).

Execution order (visible in this function, not inferred transitive effects):

  1. Set default_outgoing_field from 'is_default_outgoing_number'.
  2. Set skip_default_outgoing_check from self.env.context.get('voip_skip_default_outgoing_check').
  3. Set config_changed from bool({'did_number', 'destination_ref', 'state', default_outgoing_field} & vals.keys()).
  4. Set notify_all_users from default_outgoing_field in vals or bool({'did_number', 'state'} & vals.keys() and self.filtered(default_outgoing_field)).
  5. Set loses_default_outgoing_number from vals.get('state') not in (None, 'active') and self.filtered(default_outgoing_field).
  6. Test vals.get(default_outgoing_field). If true:
    1. Evaluate self.ensure_one(); follow the named callee for its effects.
    2. Test vals.get('state', self.state) != 'active'. If true:
      1. Raise UserError(self.env._('Only an active phone number can be the default outgoing number.')); follow the nearest applicable handler, not an assumed provider rollback.
    3. Set previous_default from self.sudo().search([(default_outgoing_field, '=', True), ('id', '!=', self.id)]).
    4. Test previous_default. If true:
      1. Evaluate previous_default.with_context(voip_skip_config_bus=True, voip_skip_default_outgoing_check=True).write({default_outgoing_field: False}); follow the named callee for its effects.
      2. Evaluate previous_default.flush_recordset([default_outgoing_field]); follow the named callee for its effects.

    Otherwise:

    1. Test default_outgoing_field in vals and (not vals[default_outgoing_field]) and (not skip_default_outgoing_check) and self.filtered(default_outgoing_field). If true:
      1. Raise UserError(self.env._('Select another default outgoing number before clearing the current one.')); follow the nearest applicable handler, not an assumed provider rollback.
  7. Test vals.get('state') in ('released', 'failure'). If true:
    1. Set vals['destination_ref'] from False.
  8. Set destination_before_by_id from {}.
  9. Test 'destination_ref' in vals. If true:
    1. Set destination_before_by_id from {did.id: did._get_routing_destination() for did in self}.
  10. Set do_sync from bool({'destination_ref', 'state'} & vals.keys()).
  11. Set users_before from self.env['res.users'].
  12. Test do_sync. If true:
    1. Set users_before from self.user_id.
  13. Set res from super().write(vals).
  14. Test 'destination_ref' in vals. If true:
    1. Evaluate self._subscribe_status_followers(); follow the named callee for its effects.
    2. Set notify_all_users from notify_all_users or any((destination_before_by_id[did.id] and destination_before_by_id[did.id]._name in SHARED_DESTINATION_TYPE_BY_MODEL or did._is_shared_destination() for did in self)).
  15. Test do_sync. If true:
    1. Set users_after from self.user_id.
    2. Test not self.env.context.get('voip_skip_pbx_sync'). If true:
      1. Test 'destination_ref' in vals. If true:
        1. Evaluate (users_after - users_before).with_context(voip_skip_config_bus=True)._select_odoo_voip_provider(); follow the named callee for its effects.
      2. Set users from users_before | users_after.
      3. Set records from self.with_context(voip_skip_config_bus=True).
      4. Evaluate records._sync_user_provisioning(users); follow the named callee for its effects.
      5. Evaluate records._sync_pbx_incall(); follow the named callee for its effects.
      6. Evaluate records._sync_user_outgoing_caller_ids(users); follow the named callee for its effects.
  16. Test vals.get(default_outgoing_field) and (not self.env.context.get('voip_skip_pbx_sync')). If true:
    1. Evaluate self.env['voip.pbx.service']._update_default_outgoing_number(phone_number=self.did_number); follow the named callee for its effects.
  17. Test loses_default_outgoing_number and (not self.env.context.get('voip_skip_pbx_sync')). If true:
    1. Evaluate self.with_context(voip_skip_config_bus=True)._ensure_default_outgoing_number(); follow the named callee for its effects.
  18. Test config_changed. If true:
    1. Evaluate self._notify_softphone_config_updated(users_before | self.user_id, all_users=notify_all_users); follow the named callee for its effects.
  19. Return res; this branch ends here.

VoipDidNumber._sync_user_provisioning

Inputs and defaults: VoipDidNumber._sync_user_provisioning(self, users).

Execution order (visible in this function, not inferred transitive effects):

  1. Test not users. If true:
    1. Return None; this branch ends here.
  2. Set live_dids from self.env['voip.did.number'].sudo().search([('user_id', 'in', users.ids), ('state', 'in', ('ordering', 'pending', 'active', 'suspended'))]).
  3. Set service from self.env['voip.pbx.service'].
  4. Set odoo_provider from service.voip_provider.
  5. Set extension_model from self.env['voip.extension'].
  6. Set settings_model from self.env['res.users.settings'].sudo().
  7. Set live_dids from live_dids.filtered(lambda did: did.user_id.res_users_settings_id.voip_provider_id == odoo_provider).
  8. For each did in live_dids:
    1. Set user from did.user_id.
    2. Set settings from settings_model._find_or_create_for_user(user).
    3. Test not settings.voip_username or not settings.voip_secret or (not user.voip_pbx_user_id) or (not user.voip_pbx_line_id). If true:
      1. Evaluate user._sync_pbx_user(); follow the named callee for its effects.
    4. Evaluate extension_model._find_or_create_for_user(user); follow the named callee for its effects.
  9. Set active_dids from live_dids.filtered(lambda did: did.state == 'active').
  10. Set users_without_active_did from users - active_dids.user_id.
  11. Set pbx_users_to_reset from users_without_active_did.sudo().filtered('voip_pbx_user_id').
  12. Test pbx_users_to_reset. If true:
    1. Set service from self.env['voip.pbx.service'].
    2. For each user in pbx_users_to_reset:
      1. Try these operations:
        1. Evaluate service._update_user_caller_id(user_id=user.voip_pbx_user_id, outgoing_caller_id='default'); follow the named callee for its effects.

        On PhoneServiceError:

        1. Test error.error_key != 'not_found'. If true:
          1. Raise the current exception; follow the nearest applicable handler, not an assumed provider rollback.
        2. Evaluate user.write({'voip_pbx_user_id': False, 'voip_pbx_user_uuid': False, 'voip_pbx_line_id': False}); follow the named callee for its effects.

    1. Evaluate _logger.warning('_handle_status_event: unknown state %r for %s', state, phone_number); follow the named callee for its effects.
    2. Return None; this branch ends here.
  5. Set did from self.sudo().search([('did_number', '=', phone_number)], limit=1).
  6. Set advanced_order from payload.get('advanced_order').
  7. Set number_request from self.env['voip.did.number.request'].
  8. Test isinstance(advanced_order, dict). If true:
    1. Set number_request from number_request.sudo().search([('request_uuid', '=', advanced_order.get('request_uuid'))], limit=1).
    2. Test not number_request. If true:
      1. Evaluate _logger.warning('_handle_status_event: unknown advanced number request'); follow the named callee for its effects.
      2. Return None; this branch ends here.
    3. Test did and did.state not in ('failure', 'released') and (did.number_request_id != number_request). If true:
      1. Evaluate _logger.warning('_handle_status_event: phone number belongs to another request'); follow the named callee for its effects.
      2. Return None; this branch ends here.
  9. Test not did or (isinstance(advanced_order, dict) and did.state in ('failure', 'released')). If true:
    1. Test not isinstance(advanced_order, dict). If true:
      1. Return None; this branch ends here.
    2. Set country from number_request.country_id.
    3. Set number_type from number_request.did_number_type.
    4. Set requester from number_request.requested_by_id.
    5. Set requirement_group from number_request.requirement_group_id.
    6. Set existing_number from self.sudo().search([('user_id', '=', requester.id), ('state', '!=', 'released')], limit=1).
    7. Set assign_to_requester from requester.active and (not existing_number).
    8. Set did from self.with_user(requester).sudo()._create_or_reuse_for_order([{'did_number': phone_number, 'state': state, 'country_id': country.id, 'did_number_type': number_type, 'requirement_group_id': requirement_group.id or False, 'number_request_id': number_request.id….
    9. Test assign_to_requester and state not in ('failure', 'released'). If true:
      1. Set did.with_context(voip_skip_pbx_sync=True).destination_ref from requester.

      3. Evaluate did._sync_pbx_after_status_update(requester); follow the named callee for its effects.

  11. Test number_request and (not did.number_request_id). If true:
    1. Set did.number_request_id from number_request.
  12. Set event from payload.get('event').
  13. Set error from payload.get('error').
  14. Set old_state from did.state.
  15. Set users_before from did.user_id.
  16. Evaluate did.with_context(voip_skip_pbx_sync=True).write({'state': state}); follow the named callee for its effects.
  17. Test 'requirement_statuses' in payload. If true:
    1. Evaluate did._sync_requirement_statuses(payload['requirement_statuses']); follow the named callee for its effects.
  18. Test old_state != state. If true:
    1. Evaluate did._notify_status_updated(); follow the named callee for its effects.
    2. Evaluate did._sync_pbx_after_status_update(users_before | did.user_id); follow the named callee for its effects.
  19. Test event == 'deletion_confirmed'. If true:
    1. Evaluate did.post_notification(self.env._('Number deletion confirmed by the provider.')); follow the named callee for its effects.
    2. Return None; this branch ends here.
  20. Test event == 'deletion_failed'. If true:
    1. Test error. If true:
      1. Evaluate did.post_notification(self.env._('Number deletion failed: %(error)s', error=error)); follow the named callee for its effects.
    2. Return None; this branch ends here.
  21. Test event in ('order_created', 'order_in_progress'). If true:
    1. Set label from self.env._('created') if event == 'order_created' else self.env._('in progress').
    2. Evaluate did.post_notification(self.env._('Number order update: %(status)s.', status=label)); follow the named callee for its effects.

    Otherwise:

    1. Test event == 'order_failed' and error. If true:
      1. Set error from {'insufficient_credits': self.env._('You do not have enough credits to complete this operation.'), 'number_unavailable': self.env._('The search result expired or the number became unavailable. Search again and complete the purchase promptly. No credits were….
      2. Evaluate did.post_notification(self.env._('Number order failed: %(error)s', error=error)); follow the named callee for its effects.
  22. Evaluate did._fetch_and_post_sub_order_comments(); follow the named callee for its effects.

Inputs and defaults: VoipDidNumber._sync_requirement_statuses(self, statuses).

Execution order (visible in this function, not inferred transitive effects):

  1. Evaluate self.ensure_one(); follow the named callee for its effects.
  2. Test not isinstance(statuses, dict) or statuses == (self.requirement_statuses or {}). If true:
    1. Return None; this branch ends here.
  3. Set previous_rejected from {requirement_id for requirement_id, status in (self.requirement_statuses or {}).items() if status == 'rejected'}.
  4. Set newly_rejected from {requirement_id for requirement_id, status in statuses.items() if status == 'rejected' and requirement_id not in previous_rejected}.
  5. Set self.requirement_statuses from statuses.
  6. Set requirements from self.requirement_group_id.requirement_ids.filtered(lambda requirement: requirement.telnyx_requirement_id in newly_rejected and (requirement.field_type != 'action' or requirement.did_number_id == self)).
  7. Test not requirements. If true:
    1. Return None; this branch ends here.
  8. Set names from ', '.join(requirements.mapped('name')).
  9. Test len(requirements) == 1. If true:
    1. Set body from self.env._('Action required: a regulatory requirement was rejected: %(requirements)s. Review the guidelines in the chatter, then click Update Requirements.', requirements=names).

    Otherwise:

    1. Set body from self.env._('Action required: %(count)s regulatory requirements were rejected: %(requirements)s. Review the guidelines in the chatter, then click Update Requirements.', count=len(requirements), requirements=names).
  10. Evaluate self.message_post(body=body, message_type='comment', subtype_xmlid='mail.mt_comment', partner_ids=self.user_id.partner_id.ids, notify_skip_followers=True); follow the named callee for its effects.

VoipDidNumber._filter_under_provisioned

Inputs and defaults: VoipDidNumber._filter_under_provisioned(self).

Maintainer's function contract:

Return live user-assigned DIDs whose PBX provisioning is incomplete.

`_sync_user_provisioning` is idempotent and level-triggered, but every
caller only drives it on a state *transition*. A DID that reaches
`active` while the PBX tenant isn't ready yet (or on any transient
Wazo/IAP error) lands active with no line and is never retried, because
no further transition happens. This predicate lets the safety-net cron
re-drive provisioning for exactly those numbers.

Execution order (visible in this function, not inferred transitive effects):

  1. Set odoo_provider from self.env['voip.pbx.service'].voip_provider.
  2. Set incomplete from self.browse().
  3. For each did in self.sudo():
    1. Test did.state not in ('ordering', 'pending', 'active', 'suspended') or not did.user_id. If true:
      1. Execute continue.
    2. Set settings from did.user_id.res_users_settings_id.
    3. Test settings.voip_provider_id != odoo_provider. If true:
      1. Execute continue.
    4. Test not settings.voip_username or not settings.voip_secret or (not did.user_id.voip_pbx_user_id) or (not did.user_id.voip_pbx_line_id) or (not did.user_id.routing_extension_id) or (did.state == 'active' and (not did.pbx_incall_id or not did.pbx_incall_extension…. If true:
      1. Execute incomplete |= did.
  4. Return incomplete; this branch ends here.
